clue.text: An early tea is arranged by head of press box

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the start of press is used
letters that are arranged are put into a new order, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor sets out an early tea next to the press box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places P beside the rearranged ENALTYAREA. 'Box' is footballing slang for the penalty area.
explanation.definitionFit: In football the marked rectangle in front of goal is commonly called the box.

clue.text: Include contents of menu and lock up

indicators.note: the contents of a word are its inner letters, leaving off the first and last

parts.note: to lock up a shop is to close it

explanation.surface: A restaurateur adds items to the menu and then locks up for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: To include something within a set is to take it in or surround it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Share beds here?

definitions.meaning: a share or portion handed out to someone
a plot of land rented for growing vegetables, full of garden beds

explanation.definitionFit: A portion handed out is one sense; a rented garden plot with vegetable beds is the British other sense.

clue.text: Bitter about love for these cards

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for bitter surrounds the letter for love

parts.note: tart means sharp or bitter in taste
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone resentful about a romance blames the cards they were dealt.
explanation.definitionFit: A deck used for fortune-telling, with major and minor arcana, is the kind of cards meant.

clue.text: Cone as once modified, for instance

definitions.text: Cone as once modified, for instance

parts.words: Cone as once modified, for instance
parts.note: the letters of once rearranged give cone, which is an example of the word puzzle being defined

explanation.surface: An old ice-cream cone has been changed from how it once was.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed by rearranging another word's letters, as cone is from once, is exactly this wordplay device.

clue.text: Foreign articles each containing toxic plastic

indicators.note: containing means the abbreviation for each holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: ea is the usual abbreviation for each, as on price labels

indicators.note: plastic means mouldable, so the letters of toxic are reshaped

explanation.surface: Imported goods, each one made of toxic plastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastic' looks like the material of the articles, but it is the signal to reshape TOXIC; 'containing' then sets those letters between E and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotic or foreign-sourced objects collected for their strangeness are known collectively by this Latin plural.

clue.text: Tempers fraying after prisoner gets time for skirmish

indicators.note: after means the rearranged letters follow the prisoner and time

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: tempers that are fraying are breaking up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Tempers fray in a jail when a prisoner is given time, leading to a scuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fraying' reads as part of the jail scene but is the signal to jumble the first word; 'after' places that jumble behind CON and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor dispute or unlucky clash, borrowed from French, can mean a small skirmish or argument.

clue.text: Dazed state of man of God leading men

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated St, is a holy man of God
a team that is leading is up, ahead in the score
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: A dazed priest is leading his congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupefied or semi-conscious condition is exactly a dazed state.

clue.text: Work, and note state of light

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work of music
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: A worker takes note of the state of the lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to vision or light, as in lenses and optics, is the adjective's meaning.

clue.text: Rationale of 'About a Boy'

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in letters
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: The thinking behind the film or novel About a Boy.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'About a Boy' look like the Nick Hornby title, but each word is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the grounds or logic behind something, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Aftershock unexpectedly divided Madeira, say

parts.note: split as afters, British slang for the pudding course of a meal
the remaining hock is a German white drink from the Rhine

explanation.surface: An unexpected tremor shook Madeira, the Atlantic island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly divided' tells you to split Aftershock not as after+shock but as AFTERS+HOCK, then translate each part. Afters is British for pudding; hock is Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a sweet fortified drink often served with pudding, an example of the category.

clue.text: Peak time with virtually all following surgical procedure

indicators.note: following means the word for virtually all comes after the operation

parts.note: op is short for operation
most is nearly all

explanation.surface: A busy time in hospital with nearly everyone after an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, peak means highest, as does the uppermost of anything.

clue.text: Dog with no tail snaffling new meat dish

indicators.note: snaffling means grabbing, so the shortened dog takes the letter inside
losing its tail means the dog word drops its last letter

parts.note: a terrier is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A dog with a docked tail steals a fresh meat dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no tail' cuts TERRIER to TERRIE; N goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pâté or coarse loaf of meat cooked in an earthenware container is this dish.

clue.text: Ale, but not Bass — that is strange

indicators.note: but not means the letter for bass is taken out of the drink

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
B is the abbreviation for bass, the low voice in music
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Ale but not Bass, the brewery, which is odd.
explanation.walkthrough: Bass is a famous British beer brand, a misleading capital: here it is the musical B. 'but not' removes B from BEER to leave EER.
explanation.definitionFit: Weird and unsettling, especially in a spooky way, matches strange.

clue.text: Corrupt cop names head of smuggling ring

indicators.note: corrupt means distorted or spoiled, so these letters are mixed up
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bent policeman gives up the name of the boss of a smuggling gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' rearranges COP NAMES into ENCOMPAS, and S is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring something is to encircle it, which is to surround it completely.

clue.text: Believer's description of one found in nave?

definitions.text: Believer's description of one found in nave?

parts.words: Believer's description of one found in nave?
parts.note: one, I, found in nave gives naive, and an easy believer is described as gullible

explanation.surface: A churchgoer describes someone sitting in the nave of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The church picture misleads: one, as the letter I, inside NAVE makes NAIVE, the description meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone too ready to believe anything is gullible or naive, the adjective's meaning.

clue.text: Sublime dish that's unfinished is site of disturbance

parts.note: epic means grand or sublime

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the dish is cut off

parts.note: an entree is a dish served in a meal

explanation.surface: A superb dish left half-eaten causes a disturbance.
explanation.definitionFit: The point on the surface above an earthquake's origin, or the centre of any upheaval, is this spot.

clue.text: Begin, for example seeing former PM ignoring leader

indicators.note: ignoring the leader means dropping the first letter

parts.note: Benjamin Disraeli was a 19th-century British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: Starting by looking at a past prime minister without his leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Begin is Menachem Begin, a Prime Minister of Israel; the capital disguises the name as the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Menachem Begin was a citizen and leader of the Jewish state, an example of the nationality.

clue.text: In snake pit a pharaoh's inscribed a message

indicators.note: in signals the letters are found inside the following words

explanation.surface: In a pit of snakes a pharaoh has carved a message.
explanation.definitionFit: Words carved on a tomb or gravestone in memory of the dead are a message inscribed.

clue.text: A step up in enterprise, really

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie within the following words

explanation.surface: Starting a business is truly a step up in life.
explanation.definitionFit: The vertical part of each stair, and loosely a single step on a staircase, has this name.

clue.text: Method of learning about place for award

indicators.note: about means the learning word goes round the word for place

parts.note: rote is learning by repetition
to set something is to place it

explanation.surface: A way of teaching about a location wins a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribbon badge given as a prize, at a show for instance, is an award.

clue.text: Save son, and curl up tightly

parts.note: to crimp hair is to press it into tight curls

explanation.surface: Rescue the boy and curl up snugly.
explanation.definitionFit: To be very sparing with money is to economise or save.

clue.text: Splitting hairs?

parts.note: the phrase usually means quibbling, but here it is the line combed through the hair to divide it

explanation.definitionFit: The line where hair is combed in opposite directions literally divides the hairs.

clue.text: Turn and explode

definitions.meaning: a bomb or alarm that detonates or sounds

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to sour, as food does, and to detonate.

clue.text: Sun's set and sailors thus open bottles

indicators.note: set means arranged anew, so the letters of sun are reordered

parts.note: Sun's here is sun is, so the word sun is the fodder; the 's gives no letter
a ship's crew is its sailors

explanation.surface: As the sun goes down, sailors crack open some bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like sunset but rearranges SUN to UNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening bottles with screw caps means twisting the tops off, which is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Daughter wearing ring, meeting over pleasure boat

indicators.note: something wearing a ring is surrounded by it, so the bell sound goes round the letter

parts.note: a peal is a ring of bells
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A girl wearing an engagement ring meets someone on a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pedal-powered craft hired for fun on lakes is a pleasure boat.

clue.text: Form found in old alcohol-free sultanate

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, drinking no alcohol
Oman is a sultanate in Arabia

explanation.surface: A shape discovered in an ancient dry Arab sultanate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' here is the bench sense, not shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A form is a long low seat or bench, and the answer is an upholstered seat without a back.

clue.text: Mean and squiffy female diets randomly

parts.note: squiffy and tight both mean slightly drunk

indicators.note: randomly means the letters of diets are mixed up

explanation.surface: A miserly, tipsy woman dieting without any plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwilling to spend money, stingy or miserly, is the sense of mean here.
